PullRequest.Title: mcp: distinguish catalog totals from page counts
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #342313.

### What changed

Preserve explicit MCP registry `metadata.total` across response serializers and use it for marketplace catalog totals only when it is a safe integer at least as large as the returned page. When no valid overall total is supplied, leave the total unknown; never substitute the per-page `metadata.count`.

This retains #342177's 99-item native request cap. Previously, combining two native pages into a 100-item Browse page produced `items.length: 100, total: 99`, which the outer `platform.mcpGallery` provider rejected and caused the entire Browse surface to fail. Legacy iterative queries and cursor handling are unchanged.

### Regression coverage

- Actual gallery service → MCP marketplace provider → platform aggregator → outer workbench-shaped aggregator, composing 100-item Browse pages from 99-item native pages and then draining the continuation.
- Both explicit catalog totals and unknown totals.
- v0 and v0.1 response handling, plus invalid totals.

### Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/mcp/test/common/mcpGalleryService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/customizationMarketplace/test/common/mcpGalleryMarketplaceProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/customizationMarketplace/test/common/customizationMarketplaceService.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 87 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/mcp/common/mcpGalleryService.ts src/vs/platform/mcp/test/common/mcpGalleryService.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Commit-time hygiene — passed for both changed files.

Environment note: the normal dependency install failed on an unrelated Foundry native-runtime download (HTTP 401). Dependencies were installed with `npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`. The Electron test runner logged a missing optional `@vscode/fs-copyfile` native binary but executed all 87 selected tests successfully and exited with code 0. Live UI and full integration/smoke suites were not run.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse the MCP marketplace with a 100-item workbench page over the 99-item native registry cap
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench aggregator calls the platform aggregator, which calls McpGalleryMarketplaceProvider and then McpGalleryService.queryPage. The first page requires two sequential registry responses because the native provider is capped at 99; response parsing and server mapping complete before the page can be returned. The added total propagation and Number.isSafeInteger check occur after the existing request and parsing and add only constant-time scalar work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: HTTP GET of a native MCP registry page followed by JSON response parsing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential GETs for a cold 100-item outer page when the first native page has 99 items and a continuation; zero additional GETs for the immediate continuation that drains the 98 buffered items in the tested 198-item catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same query loop issued the same two GETs based on item count and nextCursor. The diff only replaces the reported count-derived total with validated metadata.total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both cold GETs and parsing must complete before the first 100-item page returns; buffered continuation work avoids another request on the next page.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Requested page size and registry native page size. At the maximum 100-item combined page, effective cardinality is two registry pages (99 plus at least one item); the remaining 98 items from the second response are buffered for the continuation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: For the MCP-only source, each aggregator's Promise.all contains one active source. Registry pages are fetched sequentially because the second request is issued only after consuming the first 99 items; the diff does not add parallelism or a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold browse fills the platform continuation with the unused 98 entries from the second response and stores bounded LRU continuation state (maximum 32, 30-minute expiry). The next 100-item request is warm and drains those buffered entries without another registry request in the covered 198-item case. Explicit versus unknown total does not alter continuation keys, exhaustion, or caching; nextCursor remains authoritative.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete production diff, provider loop, both aggregation layers, request implementation, and regression test all show that totals are informational and do not control fetches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry response latency and real catalog size vary, but request cardinality and sequencing are established by the provider cap and aggregation loop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff preserves network cardinality, serialization scale, buffering, and concurrency while adding constant-time validation of one metadata scalar.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search or continue MCP marketplace results with a page size up to 99
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Manifest selection precedes one McpGalleryService.queryPage call per native result page. The initial request includes search text; continuation requests use only the opaque cursor. Each response is parsed and mapped before returning. Total validation is constant-time and does not gate or schedule continuation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: HTTP GET and JSON parsing for the searched or continued registry page
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GET per requested native page, capped at 99 servers; empty-page skipping can make up to five existing sequential attempts but is based on items and nextCursor, not total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One GET and the same full response parsing/mapping occurred per queryPage call before the diff; only the scalar returned as page.total changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The GET and parsing are on the page's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe supported registry schema version for manifests created without an explicit version
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced discovery sequence per URL, trying up to two versions sequentially; normal product-default manifests supply v0.1 and skip these probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manifest discovery and its per-URL Promise cache are unchanged and are not affected by total metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When needed, discovery completes before the first registry page can be requested.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One native page of at most 99 returned servers per provider call; additional work scales with user-requested continuation pages and is driven by nextCursor, not total.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single MCP provider performs one registry request at a time. When other marketplace sources are selected, the existing aggregator may query independent sources concurrently, but this diff does not change that fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Marketplace continuation state buffers source items and cursors in the bounded LRU. Product manifests are constructed without discovery I/O; version discovery for manifests without a supplied version is coalesced by a per-URL Promise map. The changed total is not part of a cache key and neither creates misses nor pins new collections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the request URL construction, provider retry condition, continuation state, and manifest cache were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of custom registries requiring version discovery and the number of user continuations vary; the diff does not change either multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Neither valid nor absent totals change page fetching, retries, source concurrency, or cache behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Query an MCP gallery whose query resource is a local file
Scenarios.CriticalPath: McpGalleryService reads the file, converts the buffer to a string, parses JSON, maps returned servers, and then validates the optional total before returning the page. File read and parsing are on the critical path; the added scalar access/check is negligible and non-scaling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the local registry file, decode it, and JSON.parse its contents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read per queryPage invocation, independent of whether metadata.total is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full-file read and parse occurred on every queryPage invocation; preserving and checking total adds no read or extra traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read and parse must finish before results can be returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The local registry file byte size and number of server entries. Existing parsing and mapping are linear in those inputs; the new metadata operation remains O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One file read per queryPage invocation; no added queue, parallelism, subprocess, database, network, or IPC operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This path has no response cache in McpGalleryService, so each invocation rereads the file as before. Aggregator continuation caching remains based on items and nextCursor; total does not change invalidation or retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the file branch and post-query total handling are directly visible in the changed service.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local-file registry size and usage frequency are unknown, but the unchanged I/O cardinality and O(1) added work are clear.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Existing file I/O and parsing costs are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced browse, search/continuation, manifest acquisition, nested aggregation, and local-file paths. The production change carries one optional numeric metadata field and validates it once; it does not introduce or amplify boundary calls, collection-wide work, concurrency, retention, or cache misses. No findings were submitted.
